//: Tasks run as type:process through .vscode/dev-run.cmd, which enters the VS x64 Developer
environment (cl/ninja) and then runs the given cmake command verbatim. This works regardless
of how VS Code was launched. (Interactive terminals get the same env via the VS Dev PowerShell
profile -> .vscode/dev-shell.ps1 in KLSOneMill.code-workspace.)
Use these instead of the CMake sidebar's Build/Install buttons. CMake Tools substitutes its own
selected target into every build step of a workflow preset, so 'Workflow -> Install' silently
builds only the status-bar target and installs nothing. See .vscode/OneMill-Setup-Ledger.md.
NEVER add a bare '--parallel' to these commands. CMake only consults CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL
(set to cores-2 by dev-run.cmd) when --parallel is absent; a bare --parallel makes Ninja
oversubscribe at cores+2 and freeze the machine.
The presets referenced here live in CMakeUserPresets.json, which is gitignored. Copy
CMakeUserPresets.json.example and adjust the machine paths first, or these tasks will not resolve.
'Build' and 'Install' need an already-configured build directory - 'cmake --build --preset' never
configures one itself. On a fresh clone, or after deleting the build directory, they fail with
'<dir> is not a directory'. Run the matching 'Cold start' task: it is the workflow preset, so it
configures, builds 'all' and runs install_full in one go. That is the only recovery action; there
is deliberately no separate Configure task, so there is never a question of which one to run.
There is deliberately no Clean task either. 'cmake --build --target clean' would not clean what
matters: the per-module add_custom_target(... ALL) steps copy config/, releaseNotes/ and the
ModuleWorks deps/ folders into bin/<config>/modulesBert/, and Ninja does not track those as
outputs, so they would survive. A half-clean that leaves stale plugin data behind is worse than
none. For a full reset, delete the build and install directories (their paths are in your own
CMakeUserPresets.json) and then run Cold start - see README.md.
No Debug configuration exists. It builds and installs but cannot run: static CRT gives MainApp
and each of the ten plugin DLLs its own heap, and the debug heap asserts on the first allocation
crossing a module boundary. Debug the RelWithDebInfo build - it has full PDBs.
